title: Interdependent region failover + circuit-breaker hysteresis causing sustained SLO tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-09 22:17 UTC we observed a multi-region degradation that caused a sustained SLO miss for the text-generation API (99th percentile latency exceeded 500ms for ~38 minutes). The incident was triggered by a traffic surge routed to primary region us-west-2 coincident with a KV-cache eviction event after a rolling upgrade. Secondary-region failover and our circuit-breaker hysteresis interacted in an unanticipated way: circuit breakers tripped aggressively in the hotspots, routing shifted more traffic to secondaries, which then experienced cold KV-cache priming and higher tail latency, causing more CB tripping and a cascading degrade (tight positive feedback loop).

Timeline (high level):
- 22:16 UTC: Automated deployment in us-west-2 completed (normalized CPU spike in a subset of serving pods).
- 22:18 UTC: Cache eviction and key-space rebalancing started; initial latency bumps to ~200ms p50.
- 22:20 UTC: Traffic surge from a partner integration (burst ~3x baseline for 5 minutes) landed primarily in us-west-2.
- 22:21 UTC: Local circuit-breakers in us-west-2 opened on a subset of routes; traffic shifted to eu-west-1 and us-east-1 via smart-routing fallback.
- 22:22-22:32 UTC: Secondaries experienced cache warmup stalls; tail latency grew; their CB layers then opened, causing further routing churn.
- 22:38 UTC: SRE applied temporary mitigations (reduced CB aggressiveness, elevated secondary pool capacity, pinned heavy customers to primary region) and degraded to read-only cache warming mode.
- 22:55 UTC: Gradual recovery and roll-forward of tuned CB settings; incident declared resolved at 23:00 UTC.

Root causes (synthesis):
1) Interdependent subsystems: circuit-breaker hysteresis, smart-routing, and KV-cache warmup were independently tuned but lacked an end-to-end analysis of positive feedback under surge-plus-warmup scenarios.
2) Lack of predictive warming: when a large fraction of requests moved to secondaries they experienced cold KV caches; we had no fast path to pre-warm or graceful degrade that preserves latency SLOs.
3) CB thresholds were conservative for single-region failures but not for correlated multi-region warmup; hysteresis windows were too short, permitting oscillation during bursty handoffs.
4) Insufficient capacity headroom and throttling for partner bursts: autoscaling reacted too slowly for this class of short, intense bursts.

Impact metrics:
- 99th percentile latency peaked at 1.6s (generation API), sustained above SLO (500ms) for ~38 minutes.
- Overall success rate (2xx) briefly dropped 1.8 percentage points, largely due to upstream timeout responses.
- Estimated customer-facing incidents: 24 partners reported sustained degraded latency during the window.

Immediate mitigation done during incident (what we changed live):
- Lowered CB sensitivity (extended hysteresis window by 3x) to reduce oscillation between regions.
- Temporarily increased secondary-region serving pool by 25% using reserved capacity burst.
- Pinned top 5 partner integrations to primary region for 30 minutes to reduce cross-region churn.
- Enabled expedited cache-warmup mode (short-circuiting non-critical validations during warmup) for serving nodes in secondaries.

Follow-up actions (owners and rough ETA):
- A1: Implement adaptive CB hysteresis algorithm (owner: Miguel Torres, estimate: 8) — ETA: 2026-04-10. Replace fixed windows with traffic-aware smoothing and backoff that considers downstream cache priming state.
- A2: Build a pre-warm pipeline for hot keys during failover (owner: Maria Chen, estimate: 5) — ETA: 2026-04-01. On routing handoff detect top-N keys and populate secondary KV caches proactively (probabilistic sampling + push warmup).
- A3: Add a surge admission controller for partner bursts (owner: Ravi Singh, estimate: 3) — ETA: 2026-03-31. Short-lived token-bucket per-partner to spread short bursts instead of immediate region re-routing.
- A4: Expand canary experiments for rolling upgrades to include simulated traffic bursts and cache eviction patterns (owner: SRE-Platform, estimate: 5) — ETA: 2026-04-15.
- A5: Update runbook and add an explicit 'interdependent-failover' play with pre-approved mitigations and runbook checklist (owner: Olivia Reed, estimate: 2) — ETA: 2026-03-20.
- A6: Dashboard and automated alert tuning: new composite alert for 'CB tripping + cache miss rate + routing churn' (owner: Data-Observability team, estimate: 3) — ETA: 2026-03-27.

Acceptance criteria for major follow-ups:
- Adaptive CB hysteresis validated in canary: no >10% increase in p99 latency under synthetic 3x burst while region-handoff simulated.
- Pre-warm pipeline reduces cache-warmup tail latency in secondaries by >=40% in controlled tests.
- Surge admission controller prevents routing oscillation in 90% of simulated partner-burst runs.

Links and artifacts:
- Incident timeline & notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/INC-2026-03-09-interdependent-failover
- Postmortem doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/PM-Resilience/ENG-100256
- Live dashboard (Grafana panel): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/serve_slo/multi-region-failover
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2710 (temporary cb tuning), https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/4884 (cache warmup short-circuit)

Risks and open questions:
- How to measure and avoid false positives in composite alerting without generating alert storms? (owner: Data-Observability)
- Can pre-warming introduce consistency or security trade-offs for KV data that is region-scoped? Need SRE + Security review if we push keys across regions.
- Cost vs latency: pre-warm and reserved bursts increase cost; product input required to prioritize high-value partners vs platform spend.

Meeting notes and approvals:
- 2026-03-11 postmortem review: attendees (SRE, Serving, Product, Observability). Agreed on prioritizing A1-A3. Product approved temporary budget for reserved burst capacity for the next quarter.
- Design/UX: not required for immediate fixes; console changes to show region-affinity will be a follow-on early Q3 work item.

Next steps (this ticket scope): implement A1 adaptive CB hysteresis + A6 composite alerting, complete canary test plan and schedule a cross-team validation run. Smaller tasks (A2/A3) will create child tickets after architecture spike.
